# Results — Study 896 (Risk-Parity + Trend)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"risk parity diversifies; a 200-day trend gate de-risks in sustained downtrends, so
adding trend to risk-parity improves the excess-of-cash Sharpe and the drawdown"** —
rebuilt honestly on six liquid ETFs. Inverse-vol risk budget across **SPY / TLT / GLD /
DBC**, a **200-day trend gate per sleeve** (hold the sleeve only above its 200d SMA, else
its risk budget parks in **BIL** T-bills), **monthly** rebalance, **exactly one execution
lag** (weights and gates use only information through the prior close). Both books are
raced **excess-of-cash** (each leg minus BIL). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month at build time; the sample is pinned and never creeps).
Fingerprint `003721e41f89`.*

## Data stamp

```
[data] RP+Trend six-ETF panel: 4,802 rows  2007-05-30 -> 2026-06-30  as-of 2026-06-30  fingerprint=003721e41f89
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes (`auto_adjust=True`) — SPY / TLT / GLD / DBC (sleeves), IEF (alternate bond), **BIL** (cash / gate parking) |
| Cache window | 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 (**4,802** rows, BIL's inception is the binding start), one wide parquet under [`_cache/`](../_cache/) |
| Race window | 2008-04-01 → 2026-06-30 (**4,591** days, **18.2** years, after the 200-day SMA + 60-day vol burn-in), ann = 252 |
| Rule | inverse-vol weights from trailing 60d realized vol; 200d SMA gate per sleeve; monthly rebalance; **one lag** (`shift(1)`) |
| Cash / rf | de-risked sleeves earn **BIL** (real T-bill total return); Sharpe races are **excess-vs-excess** (both legs minus BIL) |
| Costs | one-way bps × turnover (Σ\|Δ effective sleeve weight\|) × NAV per monthly rebalance; **long-or-cash — no short/borrow leg**. Sweep 0 / 5 / 10 / 20 bps |
| Survivorship | four hand-picked liquid sleeves + a survivor cash ETF; TLT/GLD/DBC are young (2002–2006 inceptions) so the tape starts in 2007 — **named on the Signal axis**; magnitudes are conditional on this one 18-year history |

## Headline race — gross, excess-of-cash both legs

| book | CAGR | ann vol | Sharpe (excess) | max DD | terminal wealth |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain risk-parity | +6.94% | 9.42% | **0.626** | **−19.95%** | ×3.39 |
| **RP + 200d trend** | +6.15% | 7.11% | **0.702** | **−9.68%** | ×2.97 |

- **Sharpe advantage** (trend − plain): **+0.077**. **Drawdown relief:** **+10.28 pp**
  (−19.95% → −9.68% — the worst peak-to-trough loss is roughly **halved**).
- **Excess-return difference** (trend − plain): **−0.93%/yr**, HAC (Newey-West)
  *t* = **−0.65** — the gate gives up a little return (it sits in cash 35% of the
  sleeve-months) but the give-up is not statistically distinguishable from zero.
- Trend gate on **63.5%** of sleeve-months; average risky exposure **0.646**; turnover
  **0.99×** (plain) vs **2.40×** NAV/yr (trend).

## Is the Sharpe advantage real? — a paired block-bootstrap of the Sharpe *difference*

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed Sharpe difference (trend − plain) | **+0.077** |
| 95% CI (2,000 resamples, 21-day blocks) | **[−0.248, +0.392]** |
| P(difference > 0) | 0.672 |

**The Sharpe edge straddles zero.** A two-thirds probability of being positive and a
confidence interval four times wider than the point estimate is exactly what an
*uncertified* edge looks like. The Sharpe-improvement half of the claim does **not** clear
the desk bar.

## Two-era robustness cut — the Sharpe edge does not hold, the drawdown relief does

| era | window | Sharpe plain | Sharpe trend | Sharpe adv | max DD plain → trend | *t* (ret diff) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|--:|
| era 1 | 2008-04 → 2017-05 | 0.502 | 0.684 | **+0.181** | −19.27% → −9.68% | +0.08 |
| era 2 | 2017-05 → 2026-06 | 0.749 | 0.722 | **−0.027** | −19.95% → −8.85% | −1.09 |

The Sharpe advantage **inverts** across the two halves (+0.181 → −0.027): all of it lives
in the crisis-dense first era. The **drawdown relief is robust in both** (roughly a
halving each era) — the two halves of the claim separate cleanly by sub-period, just as
they do overall.

## Where the shield earns its keep — crisis-window max drawdown

| window | plain RP | RP + trend |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2008 GFC (Apr-08 → Jun-09) | −19.27% | **−7.84%** |
| 2020 COVID (Feb → Apr-20) | −16.60% | **−7.14%** |
| 2022 bond bear (full year) | −19.95% | **−8.76%** |

In every sustained downtrend the gate cuts the loss by roughly half — including the 2022
bond bear, where the trend filter stepped out of TLT (long Treasuries fell ~−30% below
their 200-day line). The 2008 calendar year swings from **−2.4%** (plain) to **+10.1%**
(trend). The cost is paid in calm bull years — 2010 (−6.5 pp), 2012 (−9.7 pp), 2019
(−5.1 pp), 2023 (−5.8 pp) — where the whipsaw and cash drag give return back.

## Placebo — is the drawdown relief timing, or just holding less? (200 shuffled gates)

| quantity | observed | placebo (200 shuffles) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Sharpe advantage | **+0.077** | mean −0.049 | **0.135** |
| max drawdown | **−9.68%** | mean −17.13% | **0.000** |

Shuffling each sleeve's monthly gate in time (identical on/off frequency, no alignment
with the actual downtrend) reproduces the average exposure but **not** the shield: **0 of
200** shuffles reach a drawdown as shallow as the real gate (**p = 0.000**), while the
thin Sharpe advantage is matched by roughly one shuffle in seven (**p = 0.135**). The
split is decisive — **the drawdown relief is genuine trend timing; the Sharpe edge is
not certified.**

## Costs — cheap to run, and they don't change the story

| one-way cost | Sharpe plain | Sharpe trend | Sharpe adv | max DD plain / trend | CAGR plain / trend | *t* (ret diff) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|---|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | 0.626 | 0.702 | +0.077 | −19.95% / −9.68% | +6.94% / +6.15% | −0.65 |
| 5 bps | 0.620 | 0.686 | +0.065 | −19.97% / −9.75% | +6.88% / +6.03% | −0.70 |
| 10 bps | 0.615 | 0.669 | +0.054 | −20.00% / −9.88% | +6.83% / +5.90% | −0.74 |
| 20 bps | 0.604 | 0.635 | +0.031 | −20.04% / −10.33% | +6.72% / +5.65% | −0.84 |

Turnover is low (2.40× NAV/yr for the gated book) and these are penny-spread ETFs, so a
realistic 5 bps barely dents anything. Costs are **not** the problem — the absent
certified excess return is. What fails the bar gross fails it net; the drawdown shield
survives 20 bps essentially intact.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful (20 seeds per world)

| world | mean Sharpe adv | mean DD relief | mean *t* (ret diff) | share Sharpe adv > 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| NULL — no persistent downtrend (edge=0) | **−0.175** | +4.05 pp | −2.07 | 15% |
| PLANTED — sustained bear regimes (edge=1) | **+0.254** | +35.70 pp | +2.00 | 90% |

With no persistent downtrend the trend gate only adds whipsaw and cash drag — it *hurts*
the Sharpe (as it must); when sustained bear regimes are planted, a 200-day gate steps out
of them and lifts the Sharpe on 90% of seeds while cutting drawdown by ~36 pp. The harness
can bank a real trend premium when one exists — so the thin real-tape edge is a property
of the tape, not a blind engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED (Real on the drawdown, Weak on the Sharpe).** The **diversification /
  drawdown-control half is real on the real tape**: full-sample max DD **−9.68% vs
  −19.95%** (roughly halved), robust across **both** sub-eras and every crisis window
  (2008, 2020, 2022 each cut ~in half), and certified as genuine **timing** by the
  shuffled-gate placebo (**p = 0.000** — same-frequency random gates average −17% DD). The
  **Sharpe / return half is not**: advantage **+0.077** with a bootstrap CI **[−0.25,
  +0.39]** that straddles zero, an excess-return difference of **−0.93%/yr** (HAC
  *t* = −0.65), and a sign that **inverts** across eras (+0.181 → −0.027). Four young,
  hand-picked sleeves on one 18-year survivor tape — named.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Mechanically this is as deployable as it gets: turnover
  **2.40× NAV/yr**, penny-spread ETFs (~0.1%/yr at 5 bps), no shorts or borrow, and every
  number survives 20 bps. But what survives certification is **risk control, not excess
  return** — you adopt the gate knowing you give up a little CAGR (×2.97 vs ×3.39 terminal
  wealth) for a much smoother path, and the uncertified Sharpe edge rests on one
  crisis-front-loaded tape. A real shield, not a bankable edge — **Fragile, not
  Investable.**
- **In one line:** adding a 200-day trend gate to a risk-parity book **genuinely halves
  the drawdown** (certified timing, robust across eras and crises) but **does not
  certifiably improve the Sharpe** — the honest read is a **Mixed** signal in a
  cheap-to-run **Fragile** vehicle.
